critique: Both 0.01s and 0.08s frames are entirely black. No muzzle-flash core, orange flame, directional tongues, or residual sparks are visible, so the result cannot be compared visually to the Explosive Muzzle Flash 4 thumbnail. The intended short decay at 0.08s is moot because the initial burst is also absent.

suggestions.why: The current 5565 velocity is extreme for a flash sampled only 0.01s after ignition and can propel the burst out of the visible emission area before it forms a readable core; reducing it should keep the initial explosion on-screen.
The very high 352 field-affect-position value can strongly displace particles immediately. Removing that positional field influence should restore a centered visible burst.
A slightly longer 0.1s particle life provides enough visible duration for the initial burst to render reliably at 0.01s while still allowing a rapidly dissipating muzzle-flash motion.
